question.text: Ms. Sneha Iyer is IR head at Zephyr Mid-Market AIF. A Canadian pension fund's DD team arrives for a 3-day on-site. On Day 1 the lead ODD specialist asks to interview the fund accountant without Ms. Iyer present, review 2 months of bank reconciliations, and observe an IC meeting. Her BEST response is:

answer.text: Decline the private interview — accompany all meetings to ensure consistent messaging.
Decline the IC observation — IC meetings are confidential under the IMA.
Accommodate all three requests — private operational interviews, document review and IC observation are standard institutional ODD practice, signalling transparency and control strength.
Accommodate only the document review; refuse human interactions citing COVID-era protocols.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Standard institutional ODD (pensions, SWFs) expects unfiltered access to operational staff and governance observation. Ch 12 emphasises on-site visits and 'verify physically the existence of staff members, policies and procedures'. Managing the narrative raises red flags. **The Trap:** A, B, D all restrict access — precisely what LPs interpret as poor controls. **Cross-Exam Context:** Same open-ODD practice in XXI-B (PM) institutional mandates. The AIF version is more intense given the blind-pool commitment. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Brief your fund accountant, CFO, compliance officer and a representative portfolio-company CFO a week BEFORE the on-site. Clear, consistent, unscripted responses beat rehearsed pitches every time.
